groups.title: Purposive foundation and silent future embed
groups.proposal: Build the purposive formation as a linked, connectiveless compound whose embed is a future predicate and whose matrix expresses purposeful motion. Let the user choose Purposive as the intended construction; derive the future embed, normal silent future morph, class-conditioned imperfective stem shape, and movement-before-purpose relation. Preserve the rare sounded future morph as a clearly marked attested alternative rather than an ordinary default.
groups.writingJob: Construct a linked connectiveless purposive predicate, place an owner-issued future VNC in the embed, replace ordinary future z with silent ⎕ by default, retain the class-conditioned future stem shape, put purposeful movement before the intended action, and retain the rare sounded-s realization as a marked alternative without making examples authoritative.
groups.readingJob: Show the future embed, linked connectiveless brackets, silent future boundary, class-conditioned stem changes, movement-before-purpose timing, contrast with Lesson 28 future embeds, the rare sounded form, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the Purposive construction and may explicitly request the rare attested sounded future form. The application derives linked structure, connectiveless organization, future embed shape, normal silent ⎕, event relation, and finite continuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Later derivation and a conditional marked-alternative choice; do not add controls for linked structure, connectiveless status, class reshaping, event order, formula spelling, example stems, or a manual silent-morph switch in the normal path.

groups.title: Internal directional matrix
groups.proposal: Take outbound or inbound purposeful motion from the one final Purposive series choice. Build an intransitive matrix with stem-internal t for thither or /k/ written c or qu for hither, always after the silent future boundary. Derive spelling from phonological context and keep these matrix prefixes distinct from connective t and ordinary stem-external on or huāl.
groups.writingJob: Build the intransitive purposive matrix, map outbound to internal t and inbound to internal /k/, place the directional after future ⎕, derive c versus qu spelling automatically, keep the prefix inside the matrix, and reject analyses that treat it as connective t or a stem-external directional.
groups.readingJob: Show matrix intransitivity, outbound and inbound meanings, stem-internal location, t versus connective-t contrast, c/qu spelling unity, archaic purposive-only distribution, huāl-la-uh comparison, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user's single Purposive series choice already contains the intended motion direction. The application derives the internal directional morph, spelling, matrix location, intransitivity, silent-future order, and contrast with other t, on, and huāl morphs.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the direction contained in the single Purposive series control; do not add a second Direction choice or ask for t versus c/qu spelling, matrix transitivity, prefix position, connective status, example identity, or a stem whitelist.

groups.title: Purposeful-motion base and six series
groups.proposal: Use one concise purposive-series choice for the six licensed direction, mood, and tense compositions. Derive imperfective i with number-conditioned uh or hui, perfective o, zero finite tense, and the ordinary singular or plural number dyad. Keep the purposive o distinct from on-o and keep every typed Source stem open.
groups.writingJob: Map each licensed purposive coordinate to its suppletive purposeful-motion base, derive i-uh or i-hui from imperfective number, derive o in perfective coordinates, enforce the six direction-mood-tense combinations, realize finite tense as zero and ordinary number as Ø-Ø or Ø-h, and reject unlicensed coordinate combinations without consulting an example-stem list.
groups.readingJob: Show purposeful-motion meaning, i, uh, hui, and o suppletion, number cooperation, relation to yāuh, difference from on-o, the outbound and inbound tense systems, optative restriction, zero tense, number dyads, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the final purposive series, which concisely records direction, mood, and tense. The application derives the base allomorph, number partner, zero tense, number dyad, and all class and Source consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the single Purposive series control; do not add separate base-stem, uh-versus-hui, o-identity, zero-tense, number-dyad, class-example, or admission controls.

groups.title: Outbound nonpast and progressive contrast
groups.proposal: For outbound nonpast indicative, derive internal t plus singular t-ī-uh or plural t-i-hui and preserve both present-like and future-like motion readings. Keep purposive and progressive structures distinct; ask for an analysis only when an underspecified traditional spelling genuinely leaves both possible.
groups.writingJob: Generate outbound nonpast purposives across open Classes A–D, derive singular and plural matrix shapes, preserve typed participants and purpose timing, keep internal directional t distinct from progressive connective ti, and distinguish class-conditioned vowel length or glottal structure without using witness stems as a whitelist.
groups.readingJob: Show nonpast reading range, all class shapes, singular and plural behavior, action-after-motion versus action-during-motion, internal t versus connective ti, vowel-length and glottal contrasts, traditional orthographic ambiguity, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses outbound nonpast purposive and resolves Purposive versus Progressive only when a traditional unmarked form is genuinely ambiguous. The application derives matrix number shape, class behavior, participants, timing, and canonical form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Purposive series and a conditional Analysis choice; do not add separate present-versus-future reading, matrix-shape, vowel-length, glottal, timing, class, or example controls.

groups.title: Outbound past
groups.proposal: For outbound past indicative, derive the perfective t-o matrix, zero finite tense, ordinary number, and the licensed simple, habitual, and anterior past readings. Reuse the ordinary optional antecessive ō particle and expose a construction analysis only when an underspecified to form could genuinely be a different optative compound.
groups.writingJob: Generate outbound past purposives across open source classes and participants, derive t-o and number, allow ordinary antecessive ō, preserve the three past reading ranges, and distinguish a purposive from a connective-t plus on-o optative through typed structure and mā context rather than surface spelling alone.
groups.readingJob: Show perfective t-o, past reading range, optional ō, all class examples, purposive-versus-optative homography, mā as evidence, glottal spelling limits, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses outbound past, optional ordinary ō, and a construction analysis only where the Source text leaves a real ambiguity. The application derives t-o, number, participants, finite result, and reading range.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Purposive series, sentence particle ō, and conditional Analysis; do not add simple-versus-habitual-versus-anterior controls, t-o controls, class or witness pickers, or a surface-spelling gate.

groups.title: Outbound nonpast optative
groups.proposal: For outbound nonpast optative, derive t-i, ordinary plural h, second-person x or xi, and the licensed command, exhortation, wish, and self-encouragement readings. Let the user choose the free plural n variant and retain the rare early singular glottal form as a marked alternative; distinguish purposive and admonitive structures even where the surface is identical.
groups.writingJob: Generate outbound optative purposives across open source classes, derive subject and number shapes, license plural n only in the outbound plural optative, preserve distinctive long ī before n, keep t-i plus number separate from admonitive t-ih or t-in, and preserve the marked early singular glottal alternative without replacing the ordinary paradigm.
groups.readingJob: Show optative meanings, nonpermissive let readings, self-encouragement, h and n plurals, all class contrasts, second-person x or xi, purposive versus admonitive structure, underspecified-text ambiguity, rare early singular evidence, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses outbound optative, optional plural n where licensed, a marked rare singular variant if explicitly wanted, and Purposive versus Admonitive only when an unmarked source genuinely leaves both analyses open. The application derives all other structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Purposive series, the conditional irregular-n choice, and conditional Analysis or marked alternative; do not add controls for x versus xi, h attachment, vowel length, command gloss, class, formula, or examples.

groups.title: Inbound nonfuture
groups.proposal: For inbound nonfuture indicative, derive internal /k/ plus perfective c-o, ordinary number, and the present-through-distant-past reading range. Reuse optional antecessive ō, whose scope is the past act of purposing even with a present translation.
groups.writingJob: Generate inbound nonfuture purposives across open source classes and participants, derive c-o and number, allow ordinary antecessive ō, preserve the full nonfuture reading range, and keep hither direction separate from external huāl.
groups.readingJob: Show c or qu as /k/, perfective c-o, present and past readings, optional ō and its scope, all class and number examples, participants, and formal hither-purpose meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses inbound nonfuture and optional ordinary ō. The application derives c-o, number, class form, participants, finite result, and all context-supported readings.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Purposive series and sentence particle ō; do not add present-versus-past, c-versus-qu, c-o, class, participant-copy, example, or reading controls.

groups.title: Inbound future
groups.proposal: For inbound future indicative, derive singular qu-ī-uh or plural qu-i-hui from the selected subject number while preserving the future embed, internal hither direction, Source class, valence, and participants. Treat the displayed verbs only as evidence.
groups.writingJob: Generate the inbound future coordinate for any compatible typed Source, derive qu-ī-uh or qu-i-hui from number, preserve class-conditioned future embed shape and participants, and realize the finite zero tense and ordinary number dyad without example admission rules.
groups.readingJob: Show future hither-purpose meaning, singular and plural matrix shapes, all source classes, participant carriers, silent future embed, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses inbound future. The application derives matrix number allomorph, class shape, participants, zero tense, number ending, and finite Result.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Purposive series, Subject, and ordinary Source controls; do not add qu versus c, uh versus hui, class-example, tense-zero, number, or witness controls.

groups.title: Inbound nonpast optative
groups.proposal: For inbound nonpast optative, derive qu-i, ordinary subject and plural marking, and the licensed command, wish, exhortation, self-encouragement, and self-suggestion readings. Keep nonpermissive let readings as cues rather than additional controls.
groups.writingJob: Generate inbound optative purposives across open source classes and participants, derive qu-i, subject person, number, object carriers, zero tense, and finite form, while preserving the purpose relation and nonpermissive optative structure.
groups.readingJob: Show inbound optative meanings, command and wish uses, self-encouragement and self-suggestion, nonpermissive let, all source classes, participants, singular and plural examples, and silent future structure.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses inbound optative. The application derives qu-i, subjects, objects, number, class form, purpose relation, and finite Result; contextual English readings remain open.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Purposive series and ordinary Source and Subject controls; do not add command, wish, let, self-encouragement, qu-i, class, or example controls.

groups.title: Passive and impersonal purposive embeds
groups.proposal: Allow any owner-issued passive or impersonal Result to serve as the future embed of the ordinary purposive path. Preserve its nonactive stem and participant topology, then derive direction, series, matrix, number, and finite form without a separate Lesson 29 voice engine or a stem whitelist.
groups.writingJob: Recapture an authorized passive or impersonal VNC, form its future embed, preserve voice and typed participants, combine it with any licensed purposive series, and derive the matrix and finite result through the shared operation.
groups.readingJob: Show passive and impersonal embed structure, retained nonactive suffixes, participant changes, direction and series outside the embed, comparison with Lesson 28 future embeds, negative particles, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the Source voice and purposive series through ordinary controls. The application preserves the owner-issued nonactive Result and derives the future embed and purposive continuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Add another derivation, Voice, and Purposive series; do not add a Lesson 29 passive or impersonal switch, nonactive suffix control, example-stem list, participant-copy control, or second operation path.

groups.title: Compound-stemmed purposive embeds
groups.proposal: Recapture any owner-issued compound VNC Result as the future embed of the same purposive operation. Preserve its internal brackets, connective, valence, voice, reflexive or projective participants, and event relation; derive the outer silent future and purposive matrix without a special example template.

groups.readingJob: Show inner compound brackets, outer future boundary, outer direction and matrix, participant continuity, valence, reflexive structure, nested event order, comparison with Lesson 28, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the recaptured compound Result and purposive series. The application preserves the entire inner Result and derives the outer future embed, series, participants, and finite Result.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Add another derivation and Purposive series; do not add compound-example pickers, depth controls, manual boundary or connective controls, copied participants, or a separate recursive engine.

groups.title: External directionals and fulfilled purpose

Also allow an optional external directional on a formal purposive VNC, independently of the internal purposive direction, so the two directions may agree or disagree. Preserve literal purpose, fulfilled-purpose, metaphorical movement, and muted-intention readings without making English glosses choose the grammar.
groups.writingJob: Apply optional stem-external on or huāl outside an authorized purposive Result, keep it structurally independent from internal t or /k/, permit matching or mismatching directions, preserve all participants and valence, and retain the ordinary external-directional construction as a distinct source path that can receive a purposive reading in context.

groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an optional external directional and the formal purposive series when that structure is intended. The application keeps internal and external direction independent and derives scope, participants, form, and all compatible contextual readings.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse ordinary Directional controls and the purposive External directional choice; do not add a direction-agreement switch, fulfilled-purpose switch, metaphorical-motion switch, translation selector, example picker, or stem whitelist.
